reason: The picture links muscle-development signals to activating muscle genes in developing cells.
expectation: The signals should guide some cells toward making muscle proteins.

alternatives.reason: The other signals appear to guide cells toward the supporting-cell goal instead.

effect: The signals produced young muscle cells with muscle-gene messages, but they do not yet have the fibre bundles.
reaction: The picture makes the next protein-building step seem plausible.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and the young muscle cells have messages linked to muscle fibres.
expectation: The cells should use the building blocks to make muscle proteins.

alternatives.reason: I could start developing the supporting cells instead.

effect: The amino acids helped the cells develop muscle-protein bundles, completing the muscle goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the protein bundles appear.
reason: The supporting-cell signals picture shows another group activating support-protein genes, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: The signals should guide some unspecialized cells toward becoming supporting cells.

effect: The signals produced young supporting cells with support-protein messages, but no surrounding fibre network yet.
reaction: This parallels the muscle-cell development step.
reason: Amino acids built muscle proteins in the previous step, so they are a plausible way to make the supporting fibres too.
expectation: The cells should use the building blocks to make supporting proteins and fibres.

effect: The amino acids helped produce supporting connective tissue, completing the remaining goal. The result also showed that cells can release proteins to build material around themselves.
reaction: It was interesting to see the fibres outside the cells, unlike the muscle bundles inside them.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the supporting tissue was most worthwhile because it showed a different use for proteins: building material around cells rather than bundles inside them.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two signal-and-building-block sequences felt somewhat repetitive, although the comparison helped show the different jobs.

surprise.text: I was surprised that supporting cells release proteins into the surrounding material, while the developing muscle cells kept their protein bundles inside.

arbitrary.text: The named signals made the pairings clear, but the chapter did not explain how the signals cause particular genes to become active.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how these different cells and their materials become working tissues, though I would hope for more varied decisions.
